profiles.name: Arcanea Core
institutions: Accord Houses maintain public pact templates but cannot assign ownership.
The Polyphonic Archive stores verified encounters, dissent, provenance, and privacy restrictions.
Restoration Circles audit spirit, ecological, and community repair after contact.
laws: Spirit as an Element and spirits as entities must remain distinct in every public record.
No bond grants an opened Gate, rank, culture, mastery, or exemption from magic costs.
Accord Names are nontransferable and expire with the specific covenant.
Source-tone fingerprints may prove continuity but may never be reconstructed as commands.
Gods/Guardians and Godbeasts remain unique locked entities outside the spirit taxonomy.
bannedPractices: identity or memory used as fuel
hereditary pact obligation without renewed consent
declaring Void-aligned or frightening spirits naturally evil
profiles.disputeProtocol: A mixed circle of human, spirit, ecological, and independent archive witnesses reviews consent, provenance, harm, and release; no party may adjudicate a pact in which it owns the infrastructure.
profiles.memoryPolicy: Git-approved records project into a STAGING namespace with consent scope, confidence, provenance, privacy class, and content hash; public encyclopedia views omit Accord Names and Source-tone data.
notes: The afterlife remains unresolved; Ancestor-class entities carry explicit interpretation status.
Spirit encounters are consequential and culturally interpreted, not universally routine.

profiles.name: Darkenia
institutions: Accord Exchanges price projected spirit labor, risk, and Gate Debt.
Habitat Utilities operate cities through spirit-bearing infrastructure.
The Release Underground restores names, exit rights, and suppressed pact history.
Civic Receivership Courts unwind predatory spirit–artifact assemblies.
laws: Corporate personhood for registered spirits exists, but unregistered and collective presences remain structurally excluded.
Accord Names cannot legally be sold after the current reform, while legacy contracts still circulate as disputed assets.
All infrastructure spirits must have a funded release and succession plan.
Forecasts using spirit memory owe compensation and correction rights to contributing communities.
Shadow incidents are classified by severance evidence, never appearance, hostility, or Void resonance.
bannedPractices: artifact designs that make refusal technically impossible
profiles.disputeProtocol: The strongest valid remedy is restoration rather than asset seizure: suspend operation, preserve evidence, appoint independent spirit and community receivers, return names, fund habitat repair, and provide a technically real exit.
profiles.memoryPolicy: Public registries expose ownership history, consent expiry, repair liabilities, and contradictory claims. Private memory content remains encrypted and deletable; hashes cannot be used to recreate Source-tones.
notes: Darkenia is a working title and is not yet classified as world, realm, era, or civilizational layer.
Its darkness is institutional: coercive infrastructure and Shadow severance, not Nero or Void.

profiles.name: Community World Template
institutions: One named local Accord review body with no ownership role.
One repair body able to fund and execute release.
One archive surface that publishes uncertainty and provenance.
laws: The locked Arcanean cosmology remains unchanged.
Local spirit interpretation may vary but cannot erase agency, refusal, price, or release.
Any culture-bound source influence requires explicit attribution and review.
bannedPractices: unreviewed reuse of living sacred traditions
profiles.disputeProtocol: Creators must identify who can halt publication, who represents affected communities, who represents the spirit's recorded refusal, and who bears repair cost before a disputed record advances.
profiles.memoryPolicy: Experimental records remain outside public and canonical namespaces. Projection begins only after schema, canon, similarity, cultural-integrity, and human review gates pass.
notes: World builders must replace every placeholder institution and show how it fails under pressure.
